slides.title: Every retelling *edits the memory.*
slides.sub: What a Northwestern study found about recall.

slides.title: Recall isn't a replay
slides.body: People learned where objects belonged on a screen, then were tested. Nobody remembered every location perfectly.

slides.title: Mistakes got carried forward
slides.body: On the final test, people placed objects near where they'd put them last time, not where they first learned them.

slides.title: Old stories drift too
slides.body: The study used a lab task, not life events. Still worth asking about the hurts you replay most.

slides.title: Hold it a little looser
slides.body: Before you retell an old hurt, ask: am I remembering the moment, or the last time I told it?
